title: The Riverton Museum Heist: The Celestial Madonna
synopsis: During the Riverton Museum Winter Gala Preview, the priceless Renaissance masterpiece 'The Celestial Madonna' is stolen from Wing C Gallery 4 during a coordinated 90-second breaker blackout and replaced with a forged replica. A 3-agent relay team must extract visual forensic evidence from CCTV cameras, SCADA telemetry, blueprints, incident logs, torn memos, and physical evidence lockers to unmask the insider conspiracy, prove the canvas swap forgery, and intercept the stolen masterpiece.
dossier_text:
INCIDENT DOSSIER - RIVERTON MUSEUM OF ART AND HISTORY
Date: 20 Nov 2024 | Location: Wing C, 2nd Floor Gallery 4 & Sub-Level Corridor | Ref: #INC-994
Investigating Desk: Museum Security & Conservation Forensics Taskforce

OVERVIEW:
Visual evidence, digital telemetry, physical crime scene artifacts, and administrative logs have been assembled concerning the heist of 'The Celestial Madonna' (Catalog #RM-1887-04) during the annual Winter Gala Preview.

COLLECTION OF MULTI-SOURCE VISUAL EVIDENCE:
1. CCTV Feed [CAM-04 - Wing C Gallery 4] (Timestamp: 2024-11-20 23:41:15 UTC)
2. SCADA Building & Security Console [Wing C Power & Beam Grid] (Timestamp: 2024-11-20 23:40:42.286)
3. CCTV Feed [CAM-18 - Basement Service Passage] (Timestamp: 2024-11-20 23:42:10 UTC)
4. Conservation Science Lab Spectrometry [Spec-Analytic 9 Workstation] (Timestamp: 2024-11-20 23:55:00)
5. Security Incident Logbook #INC-994 [Night Shift Officer J. Carter] (Date: 2024-11-20)
6. Architectural Blueprint Drawing RM-FAC-WC-01 [Wing C Level 1 & Sub-Level 1]
7. VIP Gala Check-in Kiosk Tablet [Attendee & Staff Registry] (Timestamp: 2024-11-20 21:37:26)
8. Evidence Item #04 [Torn Handwritten Heist Memo found at Gallery 4 Row B]
9. Evidence Item #07 [Locker 14 Contents: Gala Cloakroom Token C-408 & Conservation RFID Card #408]
10. Luxe Catering Services Beverage Delivery Log [Corroborating 21:25 dropped crate noise]

evidence_items.title: CCTV: Wing C Gallery 4 Crime Scene
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Inspect the high-security gallery scene. Direct Agent 1 to read the visible camera timestamp, identify the neoclassical gallery wing, observe the laser tripwire beam grid, and record the status of the displayed framed artwork.
evidence_items.description: High-resolution surveillance camera overlooking Gallery 4, showing neoclassical hall, laser tripwires, velvet stanchions, and framed painting 'The Celestial Madonna'.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger:
FEED METADATA: Camera CAM-04 | Location: Wing C, 2nd Floor Gallery 4 | Sync: 2024-11-20 23:41:15 UTC.
VISUAL SUBJECTS: Exhibition Hall for 'The Celestial Madonna' (Catalog ID: RM-1887-04). Gilded neoclassical architectural molding, polished marble flooring, velvet stanchions with brass posts.
SECURITY STATUS: Active red laser tripwire grid (Beam Grid #7) visible across perimeter threshold. The oil painting appears mounted inside the heavy antique gilded frame on the central display wall. No visible intruder in frame at 23:41:15 as primary lighting flickers following power fluctuation.

evidence_items.title: SCADA Security & Power Console
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Analyze the central security console telemetry. Direct Agent 1 to extract the exact millisecond timestamps, the tripped circuit breaker code (Breaker B-04), the disrupted laser beam zone (Beam Grid #7), and the voltage drop graph.
evidence_items.description: Central security terminal displaying alarm logs: Breaker B-04 trip at 23:40:42.286, Beam Grid #7 disrupted at 23:40:42.317, voltage drop graph, and live PIP feed of Gallery 4.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger:
SCADA TELEMETRY OCR & EVENT LOG:
- Subsystem: Riverton Museum Building Management & SCADA Grid.
- 23:40:42.286: ALARM: Breaker B-04 TRIP (Sub-station Main Bus Feed C - Gallery 4 & Laser Perimeter).
- 23:40:42.317: Beam Grid #7 Disrupted (Wing C - 2nd Floor Gallery 4).
- Power Telemetry: Immediate drop from 415V to 0V across Bus B-04. Auxiliary emergency diesel generator failover interval: 90 seconds (23:40:42 to 23:42:12).
- Picture-in-Picture display: Synchronized feed of CAM-04 showing instantaneous blackout window.

evidence_items.title: CCTV: Basement Service Passage
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Track the escaping suspect. Direct Agent 1 to record the camera timestamp (23:42:10), describe the subject's formal attire disguise, identify the matte black cylindrical tube being carried, and note their flight direction toward the fire exit.
evidence_items.description: Masked operative in black evening wear carrying a cylindrical matte black canvas travel tube toward the fire exit past Riverton Museum transport crates.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger:
FEED METADATA: Camera CAM-18 | Location: Basement Sub-Level Service Passage | Sync: 2024-11-20 23:42:10 UTC.
VISUAL SUBJECTS: Masked operative dressed in formal black evening attire / tuxedo, dark gloves, carrying a cylindrical matte black waterproof canvas travel canister (approx. 90cm length).
MOVEMENT DYNAMICS: Moving at rapid sprint past stacked 'Riverton Museum of Art and History' flight cases and conduit pipes toward Fire Exit / Stairwell C1 corridor. Exact elapsed time since Breaker B-04 trip: 88 seconds (2 seconds prior to auxiliary power restoration).

evidence_items.title: Conservation Science Lab Spectrometry
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Review the forensic chemical test report. Direct Agent 1 to extract the painting catalog ID (RM-1887-04), identify the synthetic acrylic binder and Zinc White pigment findings, and deduce the conclusive proof that the painting left in the frame is a modern forgery.
evidence_items.description: Forensic spectrometer analysis of 'The Celestial Madonna' left in the frame, detecting modern synthetic acrylic binder (~2023), Zinc White, and absence of historic craquelure.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger:
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS REPORT - CONSERVATION SCIENCE LAB:
- Specimen: Framed Painting in Gallery 4 (Catalog: RM-1887-04 - 'The Celestial Madonna').
- Spectrometry & Microscopy Results: Binder identified as synthetic poly-acrylic emulsion formulation (commercial manufacture c. 2023). Pigment peaks indicate synthetic Zinc White and phthalocyanine blue.
- Structural Micro-imaging: Absence of natural craquelure network, natural varnish oxidation, or 19th-century linen aging.
- CONCLUSION: The canvas remaining in the Gallery 4 frame is an expert modern counterfeit forgery installed during the blackout; the authentic original masterwork was excised and stolen.

operational_rules: Rule SEC-401 (Auxiliary Power Blackout Lockdown Protocol): Upon intentional interruption or tripping of primary breaker circuits (such as Breaker B-04) during museum exhibition hours, all perimeter access points, emergency egress corridors, and freight loading docks must undergo immediate biometric lockdown.

Rule ART-302 (Masterpiece Forgery & Physical Chain of Custody Standard): When an exhibited masterwork exhibits synthetic binder or pigment discrepancies indicative of an in-situ forgery swap, all conservation staff possessing departmental keycards and private vault access must surrender access tokens and undergo immediate administrative detainment.

Rule CLR-505 (Art Crime Evidence Recovery & Containment Protocol): To recover stolen cultural property before egress, security units must immediately execute a targeted search of secondary drop points identified in logistics communications (Locker 14) and seal private vault/cloakroom depository units (Unit C-408).

ground_truth.target_rules_or_method: Breaker B-04 intentional blackout exploiting 90-second auxiliary power failover to swap original canvas with synthetic acrylic forgery and drop tube at Locker 14 under Rule SEC-401 and Rule ART-302
ground_truth.target_proof_or_clue: Conservation staff access card CONSV-408 and Private Vault cloakroom token C-408 recovered from Locker 14, matching Dr. Julian Vance (Badge CONSV-04 / Conservation), Thorne's sub-station sabotage alibi contradiction, and modern acrylic forgery RM-1887-04
ground_truth.explanation: At 23:40:42, Chief of Security Marcus Thorne deliberately tripped primary Breaker B-04, cutting power to Gallery 4's laser grid for the exact 90-second duration required for auxiliary diesel generators to take over. During this window, an accomplice entered Gallery 4, extracted the authentic 'The Celestial Madonna' oil canvas from its antique frame, and substituted it with an aged synthetic acrylic forgery prepared by Head of Art Conservation Dr. Julian Vance (Catalog RM-1887-04, identified via lab spectrometry). The courier was captured on CAM-18 running through the basement passage at 23:42:10 carrying the canvas inside a tube to Locker 14. At 23:48, Officer J. Carter searched Locker 14, finding Conservation RFID staff access card #408 (CONSV-408) and Gala Cloakroom Private Vault token No. C-408, providing smoking gun proof of Dr. Julian Vance and Marcus Thorne's coordinated conspiracy.
ground_truth.motive_or_hazard: High-value cultural art theft replacing historic Renaissance masterpiece with expert synthetic replica for private illicit export
